texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been following {B_nameDef} out to the hunting grounds every morning, twenty paces behind, "secretly." Today {A_nameDef} stopped hiding and asked to be taught to shoot.\n\n{B_nameDef} said to ask the council. {A_nameDef} has been waiting outside the council's door ever since, standing as tall as {A_pronoun} can.

{A_nameDef} brought a drawing to dinner of a raider stuck full of arrows, with a small figure in the corner doing the shooting. The small figure had {A_nameDef}'s name written under it.\n\n{B_nameDef}, the colony's best shot, has been asked for lessons nine times today. Most people out here learn to shoot sooner or later. The council has to decide whether {A_nameDef} starts now.

li.label: Teach {A_nameDef} to shoot
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is teaching {A_nameDef} to shoot, starting with how to hold the weapon and where never to point it. {A_nameDef} hit the target on the second day and hasn't stopped talking about it.
li.riskOutcome: Lessons have begun. The second one ended with a shot through the storeroom door, a hand's width from {B_nameDef}'s ear. {B_nameDef} is still shaken, and some of the others think the lessons should stop.

li.label: {A_nameDef} carries the game bags, nothing more
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes out with the hunters now, carrying the bags and asking detailed questions about guts. {B_nameDef} spends most of each hunt telling {A_objective} to stay down.

li.label: Not until {A_nameDef} is older
li.outcome: The answer was no. {A_nameDef} took it well in front of the council, then slammed every door on the way to bed.
li.riskOutcome: The council said no, so {A_nameDef} slipped out at dawn with a sharpened stick and came back with a dead squirrel and a skinned knee. {B_nameDef} spent half the morning searching for {A_objective}.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} show {A_objective} the messy part
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} walked {A_nameDef} through skinning the day's kill, step by step. {A_nameDef} went pale halfway through and now says {A_pronoun} wants to be a farmer.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} walked {A_nameDef} through skinning the day's kill, step by step, and {A_nameDef} loved it. {A_nameDef} now follows {B_nameDef} everywhere, asking when the next hunt is.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} found a dead bird by the wall and sat with it most of the morning, waiting for it to wake up. Then {A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} where it had gone. Not the bird, {A_nameDef} explained, the part that left.\n\n{B_nameDef} didn't know what to say, and told {A_objective} to ask the council.

{A_nameDef} has been carrying a dead squirrel in {A_possessive} pocket since yesterday, and at dinner finally asked where it went. It's still here, {A_nameDef} said, but it's gone.\n\nThe table went quiet, and then the adults started arguing. {B_nameDef} has been at it with the others ever since, and the council has been asked to settle on an answer before bedtime.

li.label: Say the dead go somewhere warm
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the dead go somewhere warm, with good food and no raiders. {A_nameDef} seemed comforted, and asked whether the food there is better than the colony's. A few of the adults think it was a kind lie.

li.label: Tell the plain truth
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the truth: the body goes into the ground, and that's all. {A_nameDef} took it calmly, but has been afraid of the dark since.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} about the ground and the worms. {A_nameDef} found it fascinating, and now keeps a jar of worms by {A_possessive} bed to watch them.

li.label: Hold a funeral for the animal
li.outcome: The colony stopped work to bury the animal in a small wooden box, with speeches. {A_nameDef} gave the longest one. Some of the adults were moved; others thought it a waste of a working afternoon.

li.label: Change the subject
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} never got an answer, and has added it to the list of things the adults won't talk about.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} never got an answer, so {A_pronoun} has been asking the question at every meal since, of anyone who will sit still for it.

texts.li: Food has been disappearing from the stores, a potato one day, a strip of jerky the next. {B_nameDef} followed the trail past the wall and found {A_nameDef} hand-feeding a scruffy wild animal, which bolted as soon as it saw {B_objective}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has given it a name, and won't say it in front of {B_nameDef}.

{A_nameDef} has made a friend. It lives in the scrub past the wall, has a lot of teeth, and eats whatever {A_nameDef} can smuggle out of the stores in a sleeve.\n\n{B_nameDef} has seen the tracks, and wants the council's say before doing anything about the animal.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} keep feeding it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} now takes a small ration out past the wall every evening. The animal is getting fat, and the stores are getting lighter.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} kept feeding it, and it started bringing others. Several animals now wait past the wall each evening, and they've started nosing around the storeroom.

li.label: Chase it off for good
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} chased the animal off with a lot of shouting and one thrown boot. {A_nameDef} watched from the wall and has not spoken to {B_nameDef} since.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} deal with it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} went out at dusk and came back wiping a knife. {A_nameDef} had been watching from the wall the whole time.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} went out at dusk to deal with it and came back with a knife and a long scratch down one arm. {A_nameDef} heard all of it, and screamed at {B_nameDef} across the yard until {A_possessive} voice gave out.

li.label: Say nothing
li.outcome: Nothing was done. Jerky still goes missing, the animal is getting bolder, and {B_nameDef} watches the scrub.
li.riskOutcome: The council said nothing, and the animal grew bold enough to come over the wall at night and clear out a shelf of the storeroom by itself.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef} bit {B_nameDef} this morning. Not a nip, but a proper bite, the kind that needs a bandage and a sit-down.\n\n{B_nameDef} says it came out of nowhere. {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} stepped on {PET_nameDef} first, and doesn't see why the animal should be punished for it.

{B_nameDef} came to the council holding up a bandaged hand. {PET_nameDef} did that, and {A_nameDef} isn't nearly as sorry as {B_nameDef} would like.\n\n"It's never bitten anyone before," {A_nameDef} says. "No one's ever given it a reason."

li.label: {A_nameDef} pays 30 silver
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} paid {B_nameDef} thirty silver for {PET_nameDef}'s bite, counting it out coin by coin and complaining the whole time.

li.label: Keep {PET_nameDef} penned for a while
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} is penned until further notice. {A_nameDef} visits every day and sits by the fence.
li.riskOutcome: {PET_nameDef} was penned, dug out by morning, and went straight to {B_nameDef}'s room to chew up {B_possessive} boots.

li.label: Turn {PET_nameDef} loose
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} was walked out past the wall and left there. It followed {A_nameDef} halfway back before it understood. {A_nameDef} hasn't looked at {B_nameDef} since.

li.label: Let it go
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} goes unpunished. {B_nameDef} keeps well clear of the animal now, and isn't speaking to {A_nameDef}.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go. A few days later {PET_nameDef} bit {B_nameDef} again, on the other hand.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef} is stiff in the mornings, off {PET_possessive} food, and sleeps in the sun most of the day. {B_nameDef}, who knows animals better than anyone here, looked {PET_objective} over and said it isn't the kind of sickness that gets better.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council what to do, and begged them not to say it out loud.

{A_nameDef} has been helping {PET_nameDef} to {PET_possessive} feet every morning, because {PET_nameDef} can't manage it alone anymore. {B_nameDef} says it will only get harder for both of them.\n\nNo medicine will fix this. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to help decide what happens now.

li.label: Nurse {PET_nameDef}
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} gets a warm corner, soft food, and {B_nameDef} sitting up with {PET_objective} at night. {PET_nameDef} is eating again.
li.riskOutcome: {PET_nameDef} got soft food, a warm corner, and {B_nameDef} sitting up every night. It bought {PET_objective} some time and cost {A_nameDef} a lot of sleep, but {PET_nameDef} isn't getting better.

li.label: Take {PET_nameDef} on one last walk
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walked {PET_nameDef} out past the walls, slowly, the long way around, and came back alone. {A_nameDef} hasn't talked about it, and the others haven't asked.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} decide
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} looked at {PET_nameDef} for a long time and decided there was some fight left. {PET_nameDef} now sleeps on {B_nameDef}'s spare blanket and eats better than most colonists.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} looked at {PET_nameDef} for a long time, then took {PET_objective} out for one last walk. {A_nameDef} had agreed to let {B_nameDef} decide, and is taking it hard.

li.label: Let {PET_nameDef} be
li.outcome: Nothing was decided. {PET_nameDef} sleeps in the sun with {A_nameDef} beside {PET_objective}, and each morning it takes {PET_objective} longer to get up.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} has done the arithmetic on the stores, and on {PET_nameDef}. "That's a week of stew," {B_nameDef} said at dinner, pointing with a spoon, "walking around eating our feed."\n\n{A_nameDef} hasn't left {PET_nameDef}'s side since. Both of them want the council to decide whether {PET_nameDef} is family or food.

{A_nameDef} caught {B_nameDef} measuring {PET_nameDef} with a length of string and muttering about roasting times.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to say plainly that {PET_nameDef} is not food. {B_nameDef} would like the question discussed.

li.label: {PET_nameDef} is family
li.outcome: The council ruled that {PET_nameDef} is family. {B_nameDef} accepted the ruling, and still licks {B_possessive} lips when {PET_nameDef} walks past.
li.riskOutcome: The council ruled that {PET_nameDef} is family. That night {A_nameDef} found {B_nameDef} by the pen with a knife, and has slept out there ever since.

li.label: Feed {B_nameDef} extra rations instead
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} gets an extra portion at every meal, on the understanding that {PET_nameDef} stays off the menu. So far it's working.

li.label: Fetch the pot
li.outcome: The council said yes, but {PET_nameDef} got over the wall before the water boiled and hasn't come back. {A_nameDef} hasn't forgiven the council for it.

li.label: {B_nameDef} apologizes to {PET_nameDef}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} had to apologize to {PET_nameDef} at dinner, with the others watching. {PET_nameDef} sniffed the offered hand and walked off, and the table roared.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} was made to apologize to {PET_nameDef} with the others watching, and blamed {A_nameDef} for it. The shouting ended in a fight.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} found a letter in the laundry and read it aloud at dinner, doing voices. It was a love letter from {A_nameDef} to someone in the colony. It gave no name, though the part about the eyes narrowed it down to two people.\n\n{A_nameDef} left the table at the word "luminous" and has been hiding in the storeroom ever since.

{A_nameDef} lost a love letter, three pages long. {B_nameDef} found it and read it out at dinner, so the whole table now knows that someone here has "hands like a summer harvest." People have been glancing at each other's hands since.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants {B_nameDef} punished. {B_nameDef} says it was only a joke.

li.label: Make {B_nameDef} apologize at dinner
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner, from the same seat and to the same people who had heard the reading.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner, then offered to read the third page, and a few people laughed.

li.label: Give {B_nameDef} the worst chores for a week
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is on the worst chores for a week, scrubbing floors and hauling waste. {A_nameDef} stops by to watch, sometimes with a snack.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} read the rest aloud
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} climbed onto a chair and read the rest of the letter aloud, all three pages, voice shaking. When it was over, someone at the table clapped.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} climbed onto a chair, opened the letter and froze. After a long silence, {B_nameDef} took it and started reading again from the top.

li.label: Leave it be
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} wasn't punished. {A_nameDef} hasn't written anything down since, and is plainly looking for a way to get even.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has started planning {A_possessive} own funeral. There's a list: the spot, the wood for the box, who carries it, and who is not allowed to speak.\n\n"Out here, that's just good sense," {A_nameDef} told the council, and asked for help getting it all ready now.

{A_nameDef} came to the council and asked, as calmly as if asking for the salt, for a coffin to be built now, while {A_nameDef} can still check the fit.\n\nAs far as anyone knows, {A_nameDef} isn't sick. {A_nameDef} says it's simply better to be ready, and the calm way {A_pronoun} says it worries people.

li.label: Build {A_nameDef} a coffin now
li.outcome: The coffin is finished and stands in the corner of {A_nameDef}'s room. {A_nameDef} lies in it some evenings to read, and the others have stopped visiting.

li.label: Hold a living funeral
li.outcome: The colony gathered to say kind things about {A_nameDef}, who was there to hear every word. {A_nameDef} cried through most of it, and seemed lighter afterward.
li.riskOutcome: The colony gathered to say kind things about {A_nameDef}, but one speaker gave an honest eulogy instead. It was the longest of the night and got the most applause.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} pick a grave site
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} picked a plot out of the wind, under the best tree, and lay down on it for a while to see the view.

li.label: Say nothing and hope it passes
li.outcome: The council gave no answer. {A_nameDef} said "all right" and left, and hasn't brought it up again.
li.riskOutcome: The council gave no answer, so {A_nameDef} walked out past the fields to choose a spot alone, and hasn't come back yet.

texts.li: Three nights running, {A_nameDef} has gotten up in {A_possessive} sleep and gone walking. Last night's route went through {B_nameDef}'s room, across {B_nameDef}'s bed, and over {B_nameDef}, who was in it.\n\n{A_nameDef} remembers none of it. {B_nameDef} wants something done before tonight.

{B_nameDef} woke at three in the morning to find {A_nameDef} at the workbench, eyes open, carefully taking apart {B_nameDef}'s best work. Asked what was going on, {A_nameDef} said "the potatoes are listening" and went back to bed.\n\nThe damage is real, and {B_nameDef} wants a lock on {A_nameDef}'s door.

li.label: Bolt {A_nameDef}'s door at night
li.outcome: {A_nameDef}'s door is bolted from the outside at night now. {A_nameDef} says it feels like being a prisoner. {B_nameDef} is sleeping through the night again.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef}'s door was bolted, and {A_nameDef} knocked on it in {A_possessive} sleep until dawn, keeping {B_nameDef} and the neighboring rooms awake.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sits up with {A_nameDef} at night
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sits up at night now, steering {A_nameDef} back to bed whenever the wandering starts. The two of them talk in between, and they get along better than they used to.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} sat up to keep watch and fell asleep in the chair. {A_nameDef} sleepwalked right over {B_nameDef} again, chair and all.

li.label: Tie a bell to {A_nameDef}'s ankle
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} wears a bell on {A_possessive} ankle now, and whoever hears it at night steers {A_nameDef} back to bed. It works, though the jingling gets a laugh during the day.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} wears a bell now, and tosses and turns enough to ring it all night. The rooms nearby haven't had a quiet night since.

li.label: {A_nameDef} can't help it
li.outcome: With no help from the council, {B_nameDef} now sleeps with a chair against the door and a boot in one hand.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go. At dawn {A_nameDef} was found well past the fields, still walking, still not entirely awake.

texts.li: When the last trader came through, {B_nameDef} saw {A_nameDef} behind the pack animals, handing over a sack of the colony's things. {A_nameDef} came back {COUNT} {THING} richer and didn't mention it.\n\n{A_nameDef} says it was junk the colony wouldn't miss. {B_nameDef} has started a list of what's missing.

{B_nameDef} counted the stores twice, then searched {A_nameDef}'s room and found {COUNT} {THING} under the bedroll. {A_nameDef} admits to some private trading: "some cloth, a few odds and ends, a very good price."\n\n{A_nameDef} calls it initiative. {B_nameDef} calls it theft, and a good number of the others agree.

li.label: Confiscate the {THING}
li.outcome: The {COUNT} {THING} went into the common stores. {A_nameDef} feels the colony has robbed {A_objective}.
li.riskOutcome: The {COUNT} {THING} went into the common stores, and {A_nameDef} went for {B_nameDef} as soon as the meeting ended.

li.label: Take the {THING} and put {A_nameDef} to work
li.outcome: The {THING} went into the stores, and {A_nameDef} was put on the dirtiest shifts in the colony. It will be a while before anyone else tries trading on the side.

li.label: Make {A_nameDef} the colony's trader
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} now handles the colony's dealings with traders, and wears {A_possessive} best shirt to do it. {B_nameDef} counts the stores every day.
li.riskOutcome: In {A_possessive} first official deal, {A_nameDef} traded {COUNT} {THING} from the stores for a fancy hat, and insists it was a sound investment.

li.label: Let the deal stand
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} keeps the {THING}. {B_nameDef} is furious, and still keeps a count of what goes missing from the stores.
li.riskOutcome: The council let {A_nameDef} keep the {THING}. A week later, two more colonists were caught behind a trader's pack animals, each with a sack.

texts.li: The fighting is over, and the story is already being told two ways. In {A_nameDef}'s version, {A_nameDef} held the line alone while {B_nameDef} hung back where it was safe. In {B_nameDef}'s version, it's the other way around.\n\nBoth want the council to settle it before one version sticks.

{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} each say they're the one who saved the colony in the last fight. Each has a fresh bruise to show and a witness who is "pretty sure."\n\nThe argument has gone on through two dinners and is starting on a third.

li.label: It was {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council credits {A_nameDef} with saving the colony. {A_nameDef} has taken to lingering in doorways in case anyone wants to say thanks. {B_nameDef} uses other doorways.
li.riskOutcome: The council credits {A_nameDef} with saving the colony. {B_nameDef} wouldn't have it, and the argument turned into a fight.

li.label: It was {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council credits {B_nameDef} with saving the colony. {B_nameDef} tells the story at every meal, with more raiders each time, and {A_nameDef} has started eating elsewhere.
li.riskOutcome: The council credits {B_nameDef} with saving the colony. {A_nameDef} picked a fight with {B_objective} in the yard that same afternoon.

li.label: Ask the witnesses
li.outcome: After some discussion, the witnesses agreed it was mostly luck and poor aim on the raiders' part. Neither {A_nameDef} nor {B_nameDef} liked hearing it, but they've stopped arguing with each other.
li.riskOutcome: The witnesses split down the middle and started arguing among themselves, and it ended in a brawl.

li.label: Credit everyone who fought
li.outcome: The credit went to everyone who fought. Most of the colony was satisfied with that; {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were not.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came to the council after dark and admitted, as if confessing to a theft, that {A_pronoun} has a spouse back home, a long way from here, who almost certainly thinks {A_nameDef} is dead.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to send word. Getting a message that far costs silver, and it's the colony's silver.

It came out over a late drink. {A_nameDef} was married once, far from here, and as far as {A_nameDef} knows still is. Back there, {A_possessive} spouse must think {A_nameDef} is dead.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to pay for a message, passed hand to hand by travelers heading that way. Out here, that isn't cheap.

li.label: Send word properly: 60 silver
li.outcome: The message went out, paid for with sixty silver and written in {A_nameDef}'s best hand. {A_nameDef} is glad it's done, though some of the others worry about who else might read it.
li.riskOutcome: The message went out with sixty silver, and an answer came back sooner than expected. The spouse was glad to hear the news, has married again, and asks for no more letters.

li.label: A short note, the cheap way: 20 silver
li.outcome: A short note went out with the next traveler, for twenty silver and a handshake. It may or may not get there, and {A_nameDef} has started counting the days.
li.riskOutcome: A short note went out with the next traveler, who came back through a week later with the note still in a pocket, and apologized.

li.label: No: a message can be followed back
li.outcome: The council refused, since a message can be followed back to whoever sent it. {A_nameDef} understood, but has been taking {A_possessive} meals alone since.
li.riskOutcome: The council refused. {A_nameDef} took it badly, walked out of the gate after dark, and was found at dawn staring at the road.
